items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: That was when I first met Django, when we had a record session under Rex Stewart’s name, which came out very well.

ctx.x: No. Well the American union was in a much stronger position. There were only — the only band with any international recognition in England was Jack Hylton’s. I don’t think any other really had much of a name before Word War II. I mean Ambrose had a good band but they hadn’t anybody that would be known in America. Whereas in England and Europe, they knew many of these American bands, and they’d been playing there. I mean I remember I also heard Hal Kemp’s band. I think Bunny Berigan was in that band and I never…

Duke played in Paris I remember going there. That was when I first met Django, when we had a record session under Rex Stewart’s name, which came out very well. But then there was six rather bleak years while the war lasted before I could come back. And my wife being an OSS and had gone to Africa and Italy and — my wife-to-be that is — I had to come back in 1946 to pursue my suit you see. But it was a rather confusing time because it changed so much.
What was your involvement in World War II?
